claims.source: We found that in a sample of randomly recorded Id2 cells (n=76), the large majority in L2-5 had a LS firing pattern (36/45; 80% in L2/3 and 28/31; 90% in L4-L5; Figure 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings from 76 randomly selected Id2 cells, as shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: 90% of randomly recorded Id2 cells in L4-L5 had a late-spiking firing pattern.
claims.source: We found that in a sample of randomly recorded Id2 cells (n=76), the large majority in L2-5 had a LS firing pattern (36/45; 80% in L2/3 and 28/31; 90% in L4-L5; Figure 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings from 76 randomly selected Id2 cells, as shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: The proportions of late-spiking Id2 cells are similar to the proportion of Id2/NPY cells.
claims.source: These proportions are similar to the proportion of Id2/NPY cells (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of electrophysiological data to histological data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Id2 late-spiking cells have electrophysiological properties typical of neurogliaform cells.
claims.source: The Id2 LS cells also showed weak spike frequency adaptation during near threshold membrane depolarizations and had other electrophysiological properties typical of NGFCs (Table 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological characterization data shown in Table 1.

claims.claim: In paired recordings of L2/3 late-spiking Id2 cells and pyramidal cells, the connection probability was 70% (19/27 pairs tested).
claims.source: In paired recordings of L2/3 LS Id2 cells and PCs, we observed a very high connection probability (70%; 19/27 pairs tested), consistent with previous observations and the hypothesis that NGFCs mediate volume transmission of GABA (Oláh et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by paired recording data from 27 cell pairs, with citation to previous work from Oláh et al., 2009.

claims.claim: The decay rate (80 to 20% of peak) of the IPSC in late-spiking-pyramidal cell pairs was significantly slower than that in non-late-spiking-pyramidal cell pairs.
claims.source: Consistent with this, we found that the decay rate (80 to 20% of peak) of the IPSC in LS-PC pairs was significantly slower than that in non-LS-PC pairs (LS-PC: 51±8ms, n=6 pairs; non-LS-PC: 16±3ms, n=5 pairs; p=0.005, two-tailed unpaired t-test).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological measurements from 6 LS-PC pairs and 5 non-LS-PC pairs, with statistical significance (p=0.005).

claims.claim: Late-spiking cells in L2-5 had the characteristic morphological features of neurogliaform cells with short multipolar dendrites and a significantly larger, dense axonal arbor.
claims.source: Morphologically, the LS cells in L2-5 had the characteristic features of NGFCs with short multipolar dendrites emanating around the cell body and a significantly larger, dense axonal arbor surrounding the cell body and dendritic arbor (Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1; n=15), consistent with previous descriptions of NGFC in these layers across several neocortical areas (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015; Kawaguchi, 1995).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by morphological reconstructions from 15 cells shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, with citations to previous descriptions.

claims.claim: The remaining Id2 cells (~20% in L2/3 and ~10% in L4-5) had either an irregular or a bursting firing pattern during low to moderate depolarizations.
claims.source: The remaining Id2 cells (~20% in L2/3 and ~10% in L4-5) had either an irregular or a bursting firing pattern during low to moderate depolarizations (Figure 3C–D and F, and Table 1) and narrower action potentials (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3C-D, F and Table 1.

claims.claim: Non-late-spiking Id2 cells had narrower action potentials than late-spiking cells.
claims.source: The remaining Id2 cells (~20% in L2/3 and ~10% in L4-5) had either an irregular or a bursting firing pattern during low to moderate depolarizations (Figure 3C–D and F, and Table 1) and narrower action potentials (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: A small minority of the non-late-spiking Id2 cells in L2/3 (~15%) were likely α7 cells.
claims.source: We also observed that a small minority of the non-LS Id2 cells in L2/3 (~15%) were likely α7 cells, a L1 Id2 IN subtype typically localized in the deeper part of L1, which has a bursting firing pattern that can be distinguished from other L2/3 bursting cells by the properties of the burst, significantly lower input resistance, and morphology (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Schuman et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological and morphological characterization shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, with citation to Schuman et al., 2019.

claims.claim: The majority (~80% in L2/3) of the non-NPY Id2 cells strongly express the neuropeptide CCK.
claims.source: The histological analysis showed that the majority (~80% in L2/3) of the non-NPY Id2 cells strongly express the neuropeptide CCK (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Depolarization of a pyramidal cell reduced the synaptic response elicited by light stimulation of Id2 neurons by ~20%.
claims.source: Depolarization of the PC reduced the synaptic response by ~20%, and this reduction was prevented by application of the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251 (Figure 4B–C) suggesting that some of the presynaptic cells innervating the cell had undergone DSI.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claims.claim: The reduction in synaptic response following pyramidal cell depolarization was prevented by application of the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251.
claims.source: Depolarization of the PC reduced the synaptic response by ~20%, and this reduction was prevented by application of the CB1 receptor antagonist AM251 (Figure 4B–C) suggesting that some of the presynaptic cells innervating the cell had undergone DSI.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claims.claim: In paired recordings of L2/3 late-spiking Id2 cells and pyramidal cells, the synaptic response elicited by neurogliaform cells did not undergo depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition (DSI).
claims.source: In paired recordings of L2/3 LS Id2 cells and PCs, we found that the synaptic response elicited by NGFCs did not undergo DSI (n=9; Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by paired recording data from 9 cell pairs shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: In paired recordings of non-late-spiking Id2 cells and pyramidal cells, DSI was observed in three out of five pairs tested.
claims.source: In contrast, in paired recordings of non-LS Id2 cells (of 46 nonLS-PC pairs tested, only 9 (20%) were connected), we observed DSI in three out of the five pairs tested (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by paired recording data from 5 connected non-LS-PC pairs shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Of 46 non-late-spiking-pyramidal cell pairs tested, only 9 (20%) were connected.
claims.source: In contrast, in paired recordings of non-LS Id2 cells (of 46 nonLS-PC pairs tested, only 9 (20%) were connected), we observed DSI in three out of the five pairs tested (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by paired recording data from 46 non-LS-PC pairs.

claims.claim: The partial suppression of GABA release observed when the whole population of Id2 cells is stimulated is occurring primarily on the terminals of the non-late-spiking Id2 cells.
claims.source: These results indicate that the partial suppression of GABA release observed when the whole population of Id2 cells is stimulated is occurring primarily on the terminals of the non-LS Id2 cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the DSI experiments showing that non-LS cells exhibit DSI while LS cells do not.

claims.claim: The majority of the non-late-spiking Id2 cells are CCK basket cells.
claims.source: These observations, together with the molecular analysis, suggest that the majority of the non-LS Id2 cells are CCK basket cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the combination of molecular (CCK expression), electrophysiological (DSI), and morphological data.

claims.claim: The morphology of irregular-spiking and burst-spiking non-late-spiking Id2 cells was similar, but quite distinct from the neurogliaform cells, with significantly longer dendrites and a less symmetrical and much less dense axonal arborization.
claims.source: The morphology of IS and BS non-LS Id2 cells was similar, but quite distinct from the NGFCs, with significantly longer dendrites and a less symmetrical and much less dense axonal arborization (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), consistent with the published morphologies of CCK basket cells in the neocortex (Galarreta et al., 2004; De May and Ali, 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by morphological reconstructions shown in Figure 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, with citations to published morphologies.

claims.claim: Eleven Id2 interneurons were identified as light-responsive in silicon probe recordings in freely moving animals.
claims.source: Applying stringent filtering criteria (see Methods), we selected 11 Id2 INs that exhibited robustly increased firing following light stimulation for further analysis (Figure 5B–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claims.claim: Light-responsive Id2 interneurons exhibited wide waveform characteristics.
claims.source: These Id2 INs exhibited WW characteristics, and were readily distinguishable from NW cells, previously identified as PV fast-spiking INs and some SST INs (Valero et al., 2021; Figure 5B and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5B and D, with citation to Valero et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Light-responsive Id2 interneurons had wider auto-correlograms than other pyramidal cells and narrow waveform interneurons.
claims.source: Consistent with this, these 11 Id2 INs had wider auto-correlograms than other PC and NW INs, similar to the overall WW group (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: The previously described wide waveform group includes an unknown proportion of Id2 interneurons.
claims.source: These results indicate that the previously described WW group (Petersen et al., 2021) includes an unknown proportion of Id2 INs.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that light-responsive Id2 INs exhibit WW characteristics, with citation to Petersen et al., 2021.

claims.claim: The majority of Id2 cells that could be identified by optotagging in silicon probe experiments were located in deeper layers (~L3-5).
claims.source: We estimate that the majority of Id2 INs that could be identified by optotagging in our silicon probe experiments were located in deeper layers (~L3-5), where the proportion of Id2 cells that are NGFC is >90% (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the depth of silicon probe recordings and the histological data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: The 11 Id2 wide waveform interneurons selected for analysis are tentatively concluded to be neurogliaform cells.
claims.source: Thus, we tentatively conclude that the 11 Id2 WW INs we selected for analysis are NGFCs, and that the Id2 cells exhibiting narrower waveform properties are likely to be non-NGFC CCK +types.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the combination of recording location (deeper layers where >90% of Id2 cells are NGFCs) and waveform properties.

claims.claim: Id2 cells exhibiting narrower waveform properties are likely to be non-neurogliaform CCK+ types.
claims.source: Thus, we tentatively conclude that the 11 Id2 WW INs we selected for analysis are NGFCs, and that the Id2 cells exhibiting narrower waveform properties are likely to be non-NGFC CCK +types.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the combination of waveform properties and the characterization of non-NGFC Id2 cells as CCK+ types.

claims.claim: Putative Id2 neurogliaform interneurons exhibited relatively consistent firing rates across all behavioral conditions, with moderately increased activity during REM sleep.
claims.source: In contrast, putative Id2 NGFC INs exhibited relatively consistent firing rates across all conditions, with moderately increased activity during REM sleep (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Putative Id2 neurogliaform cells strongly increased their firing above baseline levels immediately following the termination of the down-state.
claims.source: Putative Id2 NGFCs decreased their activity during down states to a similar extent as the other cell groups, but strongly increased their firing above baseline levels immediately following the termination of the down-state (Figure 5H, bottom;~4 s.d. above pre-down rate for Id2; 0.2, 0.6 and –0.03 for PC, NW and WW, respectively).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: The rebound in activity following down-states was observed in 64% of the putative Id2 neurogliaform cells.
claims.source: This rebound in activity was observed in the majority of the putative Id2 NGFCs (Figure 5G, right; 64% of the Id2 NGFCs vs. 7%, 14% and 1% for the PC, NW, and WW interneurons, respectively; p<10–10, chi-squared test) and was negatively correlated with the degree of firing suppression during down-states for the Id2 group (Figure 5I), suggesting that intrinsic membrane properties of the Id2 INs could be mediating, at least in part, their increased activity after down-states.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5G, with statistical significance (p<10–10).

claims.claim: The rebound in activity following down-states was negatively correlated with the degree of firing suppression during down-states for the Id2 group.
claims.source: This rebound in activity was observed in the majority of the putative Id2 NGFCs (Figure 5G, right; 64% of the Id2 NGFCs vs. 7%, 14% and 1% for the PC, NW, and WW interneurons, respectively; p<10–10, chi-squared test) and was negatively correlated with the degree of firing suppression during down-states for the Id2 group (Figure 5I), suggesting that intrinsic membrane properties of the Id2 INs could be mediating, at least in part, their increased activity after down-states.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5I.

claims.claim: Intrinsic membrane properties of the Id2 interneurons could be mediating, at least in part, their increased activity after down-states.
claims.source: This rebound in activity was observed in the majority of the putative Id2 NGFCs (Figure 5G, right; 64% of the Id2 NGFCs vs. 7%, 14% and 1% for the PC, NW, and WW interneurons, respectively; p<10–10, chi-squared test) and was negatively correlated with the degree of firing suppression during down-states for the Id2 group (Figure 5I), suggesting that intrinsic membrane properties of the Id2 INs could be mediating, at least in part, their increased activity after down-states.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed correlation between down-state suppression and post-down-state rebound.

claims.claim: Id2 interneurons fired at an early position during the up-state sequences.
claims.source: Furthermore, Id2 INs fired at an early position during the up-states sequences (Figure 5J), as estimated by the normalized rank order during the detected up-state epochs (see Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5J.

claims.claim: Light stimulation of Id2 interneurons resulted in a significant decrease in firing rate for about half of the population of all considered cell types.
claims.source: Light stimulation resulted in a significant decrease in firing rate for about half of the population of all considered cell types (Figure 6A), consistent with the broad direct inhibition expected from NGFCs.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Pyramidal cells in the supra-granular layers were more frequently suppressed than deeper layer pyramidal cells following light stimulation of Id2 interneurons.
claims.source: PCs in the supra-granular layers were more frequently suppressed than deeper layer PCs, while both NW and WW INs showed the opposite trend across lamina.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data.

claims.claim: Both narrow waveform and wide waveform interneurons showed the opposite trend across lamina compared to pyramidal cells, with deeper layer interneurons being more frequently suppressed.
claims.source: PCs in the supra-granular layers were more frequently suppressed than deeper layer PCs, while both NW and WW INs showed the opposite trend across lamina.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data.

claims.claim: A slow positive activity modulation of a subset of interneurons, and to a lesser extent pyramidal cells, was observed following stimulation of Id2 interneurons.
claims.source: Interestingly, we also observed a slow positive activity modulation of a subset of INs, and to a lesser extent PCs, following stimulation of Id2 INs (Figure 6A; darker quantiles in Figure 6B–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claims.claim: Positively modulated responses consistently lagged the negative responses following Id2 interneuron stimulation.
claims.source: Positively modulated responses consistently lagged the negative responses (Figure 6B–D), suggesting an indirect disinhibitory mechanism for the positive responses.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data shown in Figure 6B-D.

claims.claim: An indirect disinhibitory mechanism is suggested for the positive responses following Id2 interneuron stimulation.
claims.source: Positively modulated responses consistently lagged the negative responses (Figure 6B–D), suggesting an indirect disinhibitory mechanism for the positive responses.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal lag of positive responses relative to negative responses.

claims.claim: The recruitment of Id2 interneurons leads to a wide range of response dynamics throughout the cortical column, including both inhibitory and relatively slower disinhibitory effects.
claims.source: Overall, we find that the recruitment of Id2 INs leads to a wide range of response dynamics throughout the cortical column, including both inhibitory and to a lesser extent, relatively slower disinhibitory effects.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data described in the preceding text.

claims.claim: Cortical PV and SST interneurons arise from Nkx2.1+ progenitors within the MGE.
claims.source: All cortical PV and SST INs arise from Nkx2.1+progenitors within the MGE (Xu et al., 2008), and express Lhx6 during tangential migration and in the adult (Liodis et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2008 and Liodis et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Cortical PV and SST interneurons express Lhx6 during tangential migration and in the adult.
claims.source: All cortical PV and SST INs arise from Nkx2.1+progenitors within the MGE (Xu et al., 2008), and express Lhx6 during tangential migration and in the adult (Liodis et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Liodis et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Cortical CGE derived interneurons can be divided into two primary populations: VIP-expressing and non-VIP-expressing.
claims.source: Cortical CGE derived INs, i.e., the non-PV, non-SST subtypes labeled in the Htr3a(BAC)-EGFP mouse line (the 5HT3aR INs; Lee et al., 2010) can be divided into two primary populations: VIP- and non-VIP-expressing (Tremblay et al., 2016; Rudy et al., 2011; Vucurovic et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2010, Tremblay et al., 2016, Rudy et al., 2011, and Vucurovic et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells exhibit an extremely high degree of output connectivity to other cells.
claims.source: NGFCs are an interneuron type that exhibits several remarkable properties, including an extremely high degree of output connectivity to other cells (pyramidal neurons and other INs) and the ability to induce postsynaptic GABA-B responses following a single action potential (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tamás et al., 2003, Oláh et al., 2007, Oláh et al., 2009, and Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells have the ability to induce postsynaptic GABA-B responses following a single action potential.
claims.source: NGFCs are an interneuron type that exhibits several remarkable properties, including an extremely high degree of output connectivity to other cells (pyramidal neurons and other INs) and the ability to induce postsynaptic GABA-B responses following a single action potential (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tamás et al., 2003, Oláh et al., 2007, Oláh et al., 2009, and Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015.

claims.claim: CCK basket cells are a rare species in the neocortex whose synapses on pyramidal neurons exhibit endocannabinoid mediated depolarization induced suppression of inhibition.
claims.source: CCK BCs are a rare species in the neocortex whose synapses on pyramidal neurons exhibit endocannabinoid mediated depolarization induced suppression of inhibition (DSI; Bodor et al., 2005; Galarreta et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bodor et al., 2005 and Galarreta et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Cortical GABAergic interneurons are specified during embryogenesis in the medial and caudal ganglionic eminences of the ventral telencephalon.
claims.source: Cortical GABAergic INs are specified during embryogenesis in the medial and caudal ganglionic eminences of the ventral telencephalon (MGE and CGE, respectively; Wamsley and Fishell, 2017; Hu et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018), with a fraction of non-MGE derived INs originating from the preoptic area (POA; Gelman et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wamsley and Fishell, 2017, Hu et al., 2017, and Lim et al., 2018.

claims.claim: A fraction of non-MGE derived interneurons originate from the preoptic area.
claims.source: Cortical GABAergic INs are specified during embryogenesis in the medial and caudal ganglionic eminences of the ventral telencephalon (MGE and CGE, respectively; Wamsley and Fishell, 2017; Hu et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018), with a fraction of non-MGE derived INs originating from the preoptic area (POA; Gelman et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gelman et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells in L2/3 and L1 have a late-spiking firing pattern characterized by delayed firing following a slow ramp depolarization.
claims.source: NGFCs in L2/3 and L1 have been shown to have a late-spiking (LS) firing pattern characterized by delayed firing following a slow ramp depolarization when depolarized with step current injections to near-threshold membrane potentials (Tremblay et al., 2016; Schuman et al., 2019; Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tremblay et al., 2016, Schuman et al., 2019, Tamás et al., 2003, Oláh et al., 2009, and Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells fire spike trains with little spike frequency adaptation, or even spike frequency acceleration, during depolarizations close to threshold.
claims.source: NGFCs in these layers were also found to fire spike trains with little spike frequency adaptation, or even spike frequency acceleration, during depolarizations close to threshold, and mild adaptation during suprathreshold depolarizations.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about NGFC electrophysiological properties.

claims.claim: Action potentials in neurogliaform cells have a large afterhyperpolarization and a slow afterdepolarization.
claims.source: Action potentials in NGFCs have a large AHP and a slow ADP (Schuman et al., 2019; Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2009; Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996; Wozny and Williams, 2011; Kawaguchi, 1995).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schuman et al., 2019, Tamás et al., 2003, Oláh et al., 2009, Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996, Wozny and Williams, 2011, and Kawaguchi, 1995.

claims.claim: The decay of the IPSC elicited by neurogliaform cells is prolonged compared to that mediated by other interneurons.
claims.source: Finally, the decay of the IPSC elicited by NGFCs is known to be prolonged compared to that mediated by other INs (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tamás et al., 2003 and Oláh et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells in L1 have axonal arbors that extend for longer horizontal distances, spanning several columns.
claims.source: NGFCs in L1 resemble NGFCs in L2-5 in having short dendrites and dense axonal arborization, but their axonal arbor extends for longer horizontal distances, spanning several columns (Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015; Schuman et al., 2019; Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996; Kubota et al., 2011a; Zhou and Hablitz, 1996) and have been called ''elongated neurogliaform cells'' (Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2013, Jiang et al., 2015, Schuman et al., 2019, Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996, Kubota et al., 2011a, and Zhou and Hablitz, 1996.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells in L1 have been called 'elongated neurogliaform cells'.
claims.source: NGFCs in L1 resemble NGFCs in L2-5 in having short dendrites and dense axonal arborization, but their axonal arbor extends for longer horizontal distances, spanning several columns (Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015; Schuman et al., 2019; Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996; Kubota et al., 2011a; Zhou and Hablitz, 1996) and have been called ''elongated neurogliaform cells'' (Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2013 and Jiang et al., 2015.

claims.claim: A subset of neurogliaform cells in L6 originate from the MGE (i.e., Nkx2.1 lineage).
claims.source: Within the L6 Id2 population, about 60% were NPY+ (putative NGFCs), and about 25% were strongly CCK+, with about 10% unaccounted for (Figure 2). Within the Id2 NGFC in L6, a subset originates from the MGE (i.e., Nkx2.1 lineage) and exhibit a striking anti-correlated activity pattern, with peak activity during cortical down-states (Valero et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Valero et al., 2021.

claims.claim: MGE-derived neurogliaform cells in L6 exhibit a striking anti-correlated activity pattern, with peak activity during cortical down-states.
claims.source: Within the L6 Id2 population, about 60% were NPY+ (putative NGFCs), and about 25% were strongly CCK+, with about 10% unaccounted for (Figure 2). Within the Id2 NGFC in L6, a subset originates from the MGE (i.e., Nkx2.1 lineage) and exhibit a striking anti-correlated activity pattern, with peak activity during cortical down-states (Valero et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Valero et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Neurogliaform cells of CGE origin (the majority of cortical neurogliaform cells) behave in a distinct manner in vivo compared to MGE-derived neurogliaform cells.
claims.source: We did not observe down-state active cells in our Id2 IN recordings (Figure 5G), indicating that NGFCs of CGE origin (the majority of cortical NGFCs) behave in a distinct manner in vivo.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the absence of down-state active cells in Id2 IN recordings, combined with knowledge that MGE-derived NGFCs are down-state active.

claims.claim: Parvalbumin-expressing interneurons account for ~40% of the GABAergic interneurons in neocortex.
claims.source: INs that express the Ca2+ binding protein parvalbumin (PV), which account for ~40% of the GABAergic INs in neocortex, exhibit fast-spiking properties, with most projecting their axons to form perisomatic baskets on nearby pyramidal neuron soma (Hu et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Hu et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Somatostatin-expressing interneurons account for ~30% of the interneurons in neocortex.
claims.source: Somatostatin (SST) expressing interneurons (accounting for ~30% of the INs) represent a second major group of INs, with the majority characterized by an ascending axonal arbor that targets the distal apical dendrites of pyramidal cells (SST Martinotti cells) (Tremblay et al., 2016; Riedemann, 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tremblay et al., 2016 and Riedemann, 2019.

claims.claim: VIP-expressing interneurons account for ~12% of the interneurons in the neocortex.
claims.source: A third major group of INs is distinguished by the expression of the neuropeptide vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP); these interneurons account for ~12% of the INs in the neocortex and include cells that preferentially target other interneurons, particularly SST INs, and thus act to disinhibit the local circuit (Lee et al., 2013; Pi et al., 2013; Keller et al., 2020; Kullander and Topolnik, 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013, Pi et al., 2013, Keller et al., 2020, and Kullander and Topolnik, 2021.

claims.claim: Non-PV/non-SST/non-VIP interneurons account for about 18% of the interneurons in the neocortex.
claims.source: In addition to the three main IN groups described above, there remains an additional population of GABAergic interneurons (about 18% of the INs in the neocortex) that have been much less studied.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the proportions of the three main IN groups.

claims.claim: Non-PV/non-SST/non-VIP interneurons are particularly enriched in superficial layers of the neocortex.
claims.source: This IN population is particularly enriched in superficial layers of the neocortex, and includes ~90% of the INs in layer 1 (Tremblay et al., 2016; Schuman et al., 2019) as well as neurogliaform cells (NGFCs) in all layers and CCK basket cells (CCK BCs), two IN types previously identified in the neocortex that do not express PV, SST or VIP (Kisvárday et al., 1990; Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1996; Galarreta et al., 2004; Bodor et al., 2005).

claims.claim: Non-PV/non-SST/non-VIP interneurons include ~90% of the interneurons in layer 1.
claims.source: This IN population is particularly enriched in superficial layers of the neocortex, and includes ~90% of the INs in layer 1 (Tremblay et al., 2016; Schuman et al., 2019) as well as neurogliaform cells (NGFCs) in all layers and CCK basket cells (CCK BCs), two IN types previously identified in the neocortex that do not express PV, SST or VIP (Kisvárday et al., 1990; Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1996; Galarreta et al., 2004; Bodor et al., 2005).

results.result: Id2 gene expression is highly enriched in cortical interneurons that do not express PV, SST, or VIP, and the Id2 interneuron population includes cells expressing markers such as Reelin, NPY, NDNF, Lamp5, and Sncg.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C6 are supported by analysis of published scRNAseq data from Tasic et al., 2016 and Yao et al., 2021, as shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1. The data demonstrate that Id2 expression is enriched in non-PV/SST/VIP interneurons and co-occurs with known markers of this population.

results.result: Intersectional genetics using Id2-CreER and Dlx5/6-Flpe drivers with the Ai65 reporter yields labeling of interneurons in all cortical layers, with Id2 interneurons comprising 18% of the overall interneuron population in S1BF and prelimbic cortex, predominantly located in superficial layers (L1-3).
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C11 are supported by experimental data from intersectional genetic labeling (Figure 1C-F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with quantitative cell counting from 4 brains (680/3812 cells = 18%). The distribution and proportion are consistent with previous estimates from Tremblay et al., 2016 and Yao et al., 2021.

results.result: The vast majority of Id2 interneurons (>95%) are distinct from PV, SST, or VIP populations, and almost all cortical Id2 interneurons originate from non-Nkx2.1 lineages (i.e., from the CGE/POA).
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C16 are supported by intersectional genetic labeling experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3, demonstrating minimal overlap between Id2 and PV/SST/VIP populations. The data show extremely sparse labeling in Id2-CreER; Nkx2.1-Flpo; Ai65 and Id2-CreER; VIP-Flpo; Ai65 crosses, with citations to Valero et al., 2021 for MGE-derived Id2 cells in L6.

results.result: The majority (87%) of Id2 interneurons in L2-5 are NPY-expressing neurogliaform cells, with layer-specific proportions ranging from 29% in L1 to 95% in L4-5. In L1, about 30% are NPY-expressing NGFCs, with the remainder comprised of canopy cells and α7 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C24 are supported by fluorescence in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A-B, with 638 cells counted from three brains. The layer-specific proportions are clearly documented, and the L1 composition is consistent with previous analysis from Schuman et al., 2019. The inference that Id2/NPY cells are NGFCs is supported by established associations between NPY expression and NGFCs in superficial layers.

results.result: Overall in L2-6 of S1BF, 15% of Id2 labeled interneurons exhibit strong CCK expression, with Id2/CCK cells most abundant in L2 (14%) and L6 (25%). About 80% of the Id2/non-NPY population in L2/3 are CCK+ interneuron subtypes, such that Id2/NPY and Id2/CCK populations account for nearly all of the Id2 interneurons in L2-5.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C29 are supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C-D, with 165/1123 cells counted from three brains. The lack of overlap between CCK and NPY is consistent with previous work (Kubota and Kawaguchi, 1997) and scRNAseq data (Yao et al., 2021). The inference that Id2/NPY and Id2/CCK account for nearly all Id2 INs in L2-5 is mathematically consistent with the reported proportions.

results.result: The majority (80-90%) of randomly recorded Id2 cells in L2-5 exhibit a late-spiking firing pattern with electrophysiological and morphological properties typical of neurogliaform cells, including high connection probability (70%) to pyramidal cells and slow IPSC decay kinetics.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C37 are supported by electrophysiological recordings from 76 randomly selected Id2 cells (Figure 3, Table 1), paired recordings from 27 cell pairs, and morphological reconstructions from 15 cells (Figure 3A-B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The proportions of late-spiking cells match the proportions of Id2/NPY cells from histology, and the properties are consistent with previous descriptions of NGFCs (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015).

results.result: The remaining Id2 cells (~20% in L2/3 and ~10% in L4-5) exhibit irregular or bursting firing patterns with narrower action potentials, express CCK, exhibit depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition (DSI), and have morphology consistent with CCK basket cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C49 are supported by electrophysiological recordings (Figure 3C-F, Table 1), histological analysis (Figure 2), DSI experiments (Figure 4), and morphological reconstructions (Figure 3C-D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1). The optogenetic DSI experiments show ~20% suppression of GABA release, consistent with the proportion of non-LS cells. Paired recordings demonstrate DSI in 3/5 connected non-LS-PC pairs but 0/9 LS-PC pairs. The morphology is consistent with published descriptions of CCK basket cells (Galarreta et al., 2004; De May and Ali, 2013).

results.result: Eleven Id2 interneurons were identified as light-responsive in silicon probe recordings in freely moving animals, exhibiting wide waveform characteristics and wider auto-correlograms. These cells, located primarily in deeper layers (L3-5) where >90% of Id2 cells are NGFCs, are tentatively concluded to be neurogliaform cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C56 are supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5B-E, with stringent filtering criteria applied to identify 11 light-responsive Id2 INs. The waveform characteristics and auto-correlograms distinguish these cells from narrow waveform interneurons. The inference that these are NGFCs is based on the combination of recording location (deeper layers where >90% of Id2 cells are NGFCs based on Figure 2) and waveform properties, though this remains tentative as acknowledged by the authors.

results.result: Putative Id2 neurogliaform interneurons exhibit relatively consistent firing rates across behavioral conditions with moderately increased activity during REM sleep, and show a robust rebound in activity immediately following cortical down-states during NREM sleep (observed in 64% of cells), which is negatively correlated with down-state suppression and may be mediated by intrinsic membrane properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C62 are supported by in vivo silicon probe recording data shown in Figure 5F-J. The rebound in activity following down-states is statistically significant (p<10⁻¹⁰, chi-squared test) and observed in 64% of putative Id2 NGFCs versus 7%, 14%, and 1% for PC, NW, and WW interneurons, respectively. The negative correlation between down-state suppression and post-down-state rebound is shown in Figure 5I. The suggestion that intrinsic membrane properties mediate this rebound (C61) is appropriately speculative based on the observed correlation.

results.result: Light stimulation of Id2 interneurons results in a significant decrease in firing rate for about half of all cell types, with pyramidal cells in supra-granular layers more frequently suppressed than deeper layer pyramidal cells. A slow positive activity modulation of a subset of interneurons and pyramidal cells is also observed, with positively modulated responses lagging negative responses, suggesting an indirect disinhibitory mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C69 are supported by optogenetic stimulation and in vivo recording data shown in Figure 6A-D. The broad inhibition is consistent with the extensive connectivity of NGFCs. The layer-specific differences in suppression and the temporal lag of positive responses relative to negative responses are clearly documented. The inference of an indirect disinhibitory mechanism (C68) is reasonable based on the temporal lag, though alternative explanations are not explicitly ruled out.

results.evaluation: Claims C70-C72, C76-C77, and C87-C92 are supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Xu et al., 2008; Liodis et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2010; Tremblay et al., 2016; Rudy et al., 2011; Vucurovic et al., 2010; Wamsley and Fishell, 2017; Hu et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018; Gelman et al., 2009; Hu et al., 2014; Riedemann, 2019; Lee et al., 2013; Pi et al., 2013; Keller et al., 2020; Kullander and Topolnik, 2021; Schuman et al., 2019). These claims provide necessary context for the study and are consistent with established knowledge in the field.

results.result: Background knowledge claims about neurogliaform cell and CCK basket cell properties are accurately cited from the literature, including their connectivity, electrophysiological properties, morphology, and in vivo behavior.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C75 and C78-C86 are supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Tamás et al., 2003; Oláh et al., 2007; Oláh et al., 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche and McBain, 2015; Bodor et al., 2005; Galarreta et al., 2008; Tremblay et al., 2016; Schuman et al., 2019; Hestrin and Armstrong, 1996; Wozny and Williams, 2011; Kawaguchi, 1995; Jiang et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2015; Kubota et al., 2011a; Zhou and Hablitz, 1996; Valero et al., 2021). The inference that CGE-derived NGFCs behave distinctly from MGE-derived NGFCs (C86) is supported by the absence of down-state active cells in Id2 IN recordings (Figure 5G) combined with knowledge that MGE-derived NGFCs are down-state active.
